info.bio: Formada en 1990, por Selene Vigili (voz), Stefanie Sargent (guitarra), Elizabeth Davis (bajo) y Valeria Agnew (bateria), el nombre fue tomado de una pelicula titulada Seven Year Itch, agregandose la "B", formando asi el nombre como Perra de 7 años, cuando se prestaban a lanzar su primer disco la guitarrista Stefanie Sargent muere de una sobredosis, esto hace temblar el piso a la banda, creando un futuro incierto. Luego de un periodo de recapacitación, la banda decide continuar, reclutando a Roisin Dunne como reemplazo en la guitarra.

scenes.name: Foxcore y riot grrrls
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El hardcore había sido un fenómeno masculino; el movimiento «riot grrrl» introduce el «factor chica» en la ecuación de frustración, depresión, desesperación y rabia. Nace en Olympia (fanzines como «Girl Germs», el lema «Revolution Girl Style Now!») y bebe de las cantautoras neoyorquinas, las bandas femeninas californianas (Runaways, Frightwig, L7) y las británicas (Raincoats, Slits). Un movimiento fundado en las letras, no en la música: Mecca Normal, Bikini Kill de Kathleen Hanna (y luego Le Tigre), Bratmobile, Team Dresch, Hole de Courtney Love, Seven Year Bitch, Sleater-Kinney. En California, Mudwimin, 4 Non Blondes, Tribe 8, Tiger Trap, Donnas, Red Aunts, That Dog, Muffs; en el Medio Oeste, Babes In Toyland (Fontanelle, «un arte de emociones extremas») y Sugarsmack; Free Kitten y Luscious Jackson en Nueva York.

podcast.title: Postcard to Dave Grohl
podcast.body: Seven Year Bitch sent a postcard to Dave Grohl following Kurt Cobain's suicide, understanding the grief he was experiencing. The message on the postcard encouraged him to continue with music: "We know what you're going through. The desire to play music is gone for now, but it will return. Don't worry." This message was a "deciding factor" in convincing Dave to keep making music. "It read, We know what you're going through. The desire to play music is gone for now, but it will return. Don't worry."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragedy and Perseverance
podcast.body: This Seattle band experienced significant hardships. In 1992, one of their members overdosed and died. The following year, in 1993, another member was kidnapped, raped, and murdered. Despite these tragedies, the band chose to "stick together and continued to make music," serving as an inspiration to Dave Grohl. "In 1992, one of their members O.D. and died. And then in 1993, another member was kidnapped, raped, and murdered."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ultra-Deep Background on Dave Grohl: Part 2

xref.title: Encouragement from Seven Year Bitch Postcard (1994)
xref.body: The deciding factor in Dave Grohl's decision to continue making music after Kurt Cobain's suicide was a postcard he received from the Seattle band Seven Year Bitch. The band had endured significant tragedy themselves, losing a member to an overdose in 1992 and another to kidnapping, rape, and murder in 1993, yet they continued to make music. Their postcard read, "We know what you're going through. The desire to play music is gone for now, but it will return. Don't worry." This message convinced Dave that he was "put on this planet to make music" and that stopping would be wrong. "This convinced Dave that he needed to keep going."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
